El primer título de Gabriel Knight me conquistó al instante en su día y lo colocaría sin dudarlo en lo más alto junto a obras maestras del género de la aventura gráfica como Broken Sword. Ese entusiasmo me llevó a probar rápidamente esta secuela hace tiempo, también muy elogiada por la crítica experta. Sin embargo, el cambio a FMV me disgustó bastante, la dificultad del juego acompañada a las cinemáticas sin subtítulos tampoco ayudaron y las señalizaciones, los diálogos y los nombres en alemán terminaron definitivamente con mi paciencia, fue una experiencia amarga y no pasé del primer capítulo en ese intento. 

Hace poco decidí darle una nueva oportunidad con un parche al español y aunque el principio se me ha vuelto a hacer un poco coñazo y desesperante, una vez superado ese primer capítulo la historia va ganando muchísimo porque se enriquece con un contexto histórico interesante, el cual está elaborado a la perfección en las fases de investigación y de documentación bibliotecaria, cuando manejamos al personaje de Grace. Esa decisión de intercalar las aventuras de Gabriel en Munich con las de su ayudante en las zonas más rurales sí que me ha aparecido un acierto que le da una ventaja al videojuego con respecto a su predecesor. Los encuentros con la policía y con los miembros del club también van ganando en intensidad volviendo el caso más interesante y los puzzles se resuelven con una mayor fluidez ¡Gracias a Dios! Al descubrir todo esto entiendo su fama, pero sigo sintiendo que ha envejecido un poco mal.

Gabriel Knight's first title instantly captivated me, and I would undoubtedly place it alongside masterpieces of the graphic adventure genre like Broken Sword. That enthusiasm led me to quickly try this sequel some time ago, which was also highly praised by critics. However, the switch to FMV gameplay was quite disappointing. The game's difficulty, coupled with the lack of subtitles in the cutscenes, didn't help matters, and the German signage, dialogue, and names finally exhausted my patience. It was a bitter experience, and I didn't get past the first chapter on that attempt.

I recently decided to give it another try with a Spanish patch, and although the beginning was once again a bit of a drag and frustrating, once I got past that first chapter the story improved considerably. It was enriched by an interesting historical context, which is perfectly crafted in the investigation and library research phases when we control Grace. The decision to alternate Gabriel's adventures in Munich with those of his assistant in the more rural areas was definitely a success, giving the game an edge over its predecessor. The encounters with the police and the club members also become more intense, making the case more interesting, and the puzzles are solved much more smoothly—thank goodness! After discovering all this, I understand its fame, but I still feel it hasn't aged well.

The Beast Within: A Gabriel Knight Mystery é o segundo jogo da série Gabriel Knight, mas que fora algumas informações contextuais envolvendo as relações entre personagens e o papel do protagonista pode ser jogado de maneira isolada, cada um destes primeiros jogos acaba abordando um caso diferente, quase como se fossem episódios de uma série de "monstro da semana" como Arquivo X, Supernatural e Buffy.

Neste jogo vemos a segunda aventura de Gabriel, investigando assassinatos possivelmente cometidos por um lobisomem na Alemanha, porém ele não está sozinho: nessa sequência jogamos também como a Gracie, a assistente dele do primeiro jogo, que aqui ganha um papel bem maior. O jogo possui um tom diferente, um pouco menos humoroso e mais sombrio do que seu antecessor, porém sua essência permanece a mesma: uma narrativa com elementos de aventura, terror, romance e História. Os personagens seguem bem divertidos de acompanhar, e a narrativa continua muito bem escrita - e até possui alguns subtextos que me surpreenderam muito pra um jogo dos anos 90.

O maior diferencial da vez, e o que chama a atenção de cara quando você vê imagens do jogo, são seus visuais FMV que substituem a pixel art do original. Isso também significou a troca dos atores que interpretam os personagens, sendo que os dubladores do original não necessariamente se pareciam com os personagens. Essa troca de estilo visual pode causar um pouco de estranhamento no início, mas uma vez que ele passa, eu diria que funciona surpreendentemente bem: os novos atores que interpretam o Gabriel e a Gracie são ótimos, e os visuais e a atuação que poderiam ser risíveis se encaixam muito bem com o material - ainda existe aquele charme de algo datado ou "bobo", porém nos momentos em que o jogo quer ser sério ele consegue, o nível de produção aqui é bem alto.

Quanto à gameplay, ela se mantém a de um point-and-click tradicional, com todos seus pontos positivos e negativos - existem aqui instâncias de objetos escondidos demais no cenário, diagramação um pouco confusa sobre onde você pode ir em determinada tela, ou quebra-cabeças que poderiam ter tido pistas melhores no texto do jogo, mas num geral eu diria que o jogo é bem direto e até mais fácil do que o primeiro.

Eu gostei bastante do meu tempo jogando The Beast Within, e acredito que qualquer um que seja fã de jogos Adventure point-and-click antigos e especialmente os que jogaram o primeiro jogo vão gostar bastante da experiência também. Seus visuais podem ser um pouco difíceis de se habituar para um público moderno, mas mesmo assim sugiro que deem uma chance.

i adore 90s FMV games & this one is fantastic! it's clear that so much care went into creating this game from the graphics, backgrounds, and assets to the dialogue and lore/story.
i played most of the first gabriel knight game before starting this one (sins of the fathers) but i did not complete it due to some technical issues. i would generally recommend playing it first or maybe watching a playthrough because it was definitely helpful to have the background context for gabriel & grace's dynamic and some lore stuff like why gabriel ended up in germany and what it means that gabriel is a schattenjäger, as well as some fun in-jokes and references to characters/situations in the first game. but i do think the beast within would work fine if you hadn't played the previous game, and the mystery itself does not rely upon knowledge learned in the previous game. without getting into spoiler territory, the core mystery is really satisfying to unravel, the characters are well-acted and entertaining, and the split protagonist situation adds so much good flavor and drama. 
puzzle-wise, it can be quite challenging and mildly frustrating at times, i had to rely on an online hint guide to figure out what i was missing in several parts of the game, but that's to be expected from point & click mysteries from this era. the only part of the game where i felt actually frustrated was [spoiler] during the chapter where you are first exploring neuschwanstein as grace and have to listen to the audio tapes for every room in the castle as well as tapes describing all the artwork, because it's extremely easy to miss something and not realize it, so i got stuck for a while relistening to a lot of the same long audio files over and over again. several of the rooms also require you to click the audio tape button multiple times for additional lore, but there's no indicator for which rooms have multiple audio files. there are also some difficult-to-notice room transitions in a couple other areas during exploration with grace. thankfully her journal helped a lot with this problem as you can kind of tell when there's information missing on a specific topic when there's empty space on a page, so if you pay attention to where you got information on a topic, you can kind of retrace your steps and double check everything else in that room/area. [/spoiler] 
i would recommend it to anyone who enjoys games of this era and doesnt mind a little clunkiness, or to someone who's curious about FMV games, loves a good mystery, & doesn't mind potentially needing to rely on a guide or hints to get through some of the tougher sections. it takes some patience but it's very worth it!

Bestselling novelist Gabriel Knight inherits a castle in Bavaria, where his ancestors came from. He also becomes the shadow hunter who fights evil in various forms. This time, local residents from the nearby village ask him to solve a girl's murder, and Gabriel gets to work.

You control both Gabriel and his assistant Grace Nakimura, who each solve the case together in different environments and are in contact with letters. The characters are well laid out and longer cutscenes add to the suspense. You take control in the usual point and click gameplay.

This game is a bit old, but has aged well and is still very playable. I recommend purchasing in a bundle or in a discount campaign. Have fun!

Ingredients

    1/2 cup butter, softened
    1/2 cup vegetable oil
    1/2 cup confectioners' sugar
    2 large eggs, room temperature
    1 teaspoon almond extract
    1 to 3 drops green food coloring
    2 cups all-purpose flour
    1 package (3.4 ounces) instant pistachio pudding mix
    1/2 teaspoon baking soda
    1/2 teaspoon cream of tartar
    1/8 teaspoon salt
    1/2 cup chopped pistachios or pecans
    1/2 cup green colored sugar

Directions

TLDR: Overly dramatic, Long winded, and Boring. 

[b][u]General Thoughts/Overview:[/u][/b]

It’s been almost 30 years since I last played this. It’s funny, I remember it as a visually stunning masterpiece with an intricate story and an emotional heart that was both beautiful and moving. Man, I wish I’d left the view of The Beast Within to preteen me, I’ve actually kept the 6 cd’s and transported them thousands of miles as I moved around. 
An FMV (full motion video – basically using film of actors to play out scenes) point and click adventure, The Beast Within finds Gabriel Knight, now a successful author, on a new quest as the shadow hunter, setting out from his family castle in Germany. 

[b][u]Pros:[/u][/b]
[list][*] Surprisingly well acted and scored. It is ham fisted, and overly dramatic… but it feels like it’s [i]meant[/i] to be. 10 year old me 100% bought in and loved all, 40 year old me not so much. But the characters are consistent, the music is fantastic, and it feels like it was put together exactly as intended. 
[*] The puzzles are interesting and mostly logical, with a few exceptions and a single caveat I’ll get to in the cons.  They mostly fit the theme and progress the story logically, with only a couple feeling arbitrary to plot progression. Speaking of which…
[*] The story is a fascinating mixture of real life and fiction. I really enjoyed the blending of the tragic tale of the Mad King, it was so easy to slide the mystical details in amongst the truth that I found myself extremely immersed. 
[/list]

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
[list][*] The medium by which this tale is delivered is wrong. The massive pauses between clicking and actions as the videos are located, buffered, and played is tedious. The extremely longwinded cut scenes are dull at best, and that every step of every puzzle has one is just a time killer. I truly believe that if all the unnecessary pauses, looking to the camera, and panning shots were killed, the game would be less than half the length. Combine this with the ludicrous speed the idle animations are played at and it kills the tone of the game, very, very, effectively. It’s a real shame. This would have been an interesting story delivered as a film, and a really nice adventure game delivered by animation. Here it got the worst of both worlds. 
[*] Things out of order… Out of order, everywhere. The most frustrating part of TBW is that several puzzles will allow you to try a correct combination, only to say mmm nah, and then allow the same combination after a cut scene has played later… even though it [i]changed absolutely nothing[/i]. There are also several locations which do nothing except permit a very specific action at a very specific time… And will not do so unless specific criteria are met, despite the logic of it being questionable at best. 
[*] Grace is insufferable and Gab is an idiot. They really took the characters to the extreme, and it felt wrong. Grace is a know-it-all, but she never felt like an arrogant prick… Here she feels it. Gab was head strong, but he wasn’t a bumbling fool. Here he feels it. I feel very strongly like they assassinated both characters for the sake of drama, and I didn’t enjoy it. 
[*] Game crashes a whole bunch. Every 20 minutes or so it just goes bllllllllggggrrrrreeeee and nopes out. 
[/list]

[b][u]Suggested improvements:[/u][/b]
 [list][*] Auto saving program would help.
[*] Able to skip single lines instead of entire cutscenes would be nice. I ended up getting bored and skipping half of the vast majority of the cutscenes. I then needed to go back to frustratedly and boredly watch the entire things because they held story vital points that were not recapped anywhere. 
[*] There is a single point you can dead save yourself if you’ve missed something (or only one that I noticed, at least.) While it allows you to try again, when I hit the try again buttons it crashed. every time. So yeah, fix that. (Actually, and need it be said? FIX THE CRASHING IN GENERAL)
[/list]


[b][u]Overall Recommendation:[/u][/b]

I wish I hadn’t played this. Not because it’s terrible, it isn’t, but because I remembered it being amazing…. and it isn’t. 

This game isn’t for newcomers to PnC, though I doubt any newcomers would be finding themselves here. It isn’t for people who want a well-paced and tight gaming experience, and it isn’t for people who dislike overacting. 

TBW is for folks looking for a story rich, immersive, and interesting adventure. 

Overall I can’t recommend this [b]game[/b]. 
While I do entirely recommend this [b]story[/b]. 

If The Beast Within ever gets remade into something a little slicker, with less long winded cutscenes, and the acting turned down to 7 I’ll be the first in line… Sadly I don’t see that happening, and unfortunately this interesting and lovingly crafted idea will no doubt remain a cult classic.

Although this is a very old game, it is still packs a lot of interest for me. I especially enjoy the live action factor in a puzzle game. Although it is very low rez, you can still see facial expressions on the actors and other details with plenty of clarity. I change my monitor resolution to the lowest possible (800x600 in my case) and then play it windowed rather than full screen. The puzzles and clues are interesting, the story is excellent, and for those who like using walk-throughs, there is a pretty decent one here on Steam. I hope you enjoy!
